Class LogEncoder.Buffer.DirectByteBufferBuffer

java.lang.Object
io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogEncoder.Buffer.DirectByteBufferBuffer
All Implemented Interfaces:
LogEncoder.Buffer, AutoCloseable
Enclosing interface:
LogEncoder.Buffer
public static final class LogEncoder.Buffer.DirectByteBufferBuffer extends Object implements LogEncoder.Buffer
A buffer that formats into a reused StringBuilder (like LogEncoder.Buffer.StringBuilderBuffer) but encodes directly into a reused ByteBuffer via a CharsetEncoder, instead of going through an intermediate String and byte[] the way LogOutput.write(LogEvent, String)'s default implementation does. This is the same technique Log4j2's garbage-free logging uses.

The CharsetEncoder work happens in encodeToByteBuffer(), called by the encoder's encode(LogEvent, Buffer) step - i.e. before drain, which appenders that separate formatting from writing (LockThreadLocalBufferLogAppender, SynchronizedThreadLocalBufferLogAppender) call outside their lock. drain - called from inside the lock - therefore does nothing but write the already-encoded bytes, matching how Log4j2 confines the actual character-to-byte transcoding to a thread-local scratch buffer and synchronizes only the final copy into the shared destination.

Constructed for a specific LogOutput.WriteMethod - either LogOutput.WriteMethod.BYTE_BUFFER, in which case drain(LogOutput, LogEvent) calls LogOutput.write(LogEvent, ByteBuffer, LogOutput.ContentType) directly, or LogOutput.WriteMethod.BYTES, in which case drain(LogOutput, LogEvent) calls LogOutput.write(LogEvent, byte[], int, int, LogOutput.ContentType) using the backing array directly, rather than going through LogOutput#write(LogEvent, ByteBuffer, ContentType)'s default implementation (which would allocate a fresh byte[] copy every call for an output that does not itself implement that overload).

Not thread-safe. Like all LogEncoder.Buffers it relies on the appender to guarantee no overlapping use.

    • DirectByteBufferBuffer

      public DirectByteBufferBuffer(LogOutput.WriteMethod writeMethod, int initialByteCapacity, Charset charset)
      Creates a buffer with the given write method, initial byte capacity and charset.
      Parameters:
      writeMethod - which LogOutput.write(LogEvent[], int, LogEncoder) overload drain(LogOutput, LogEvent) should call - LogOutput.WriteMethod.BYTES or LogOutput.WriteMethod.BYTE_BUFFER.
      initialByteCapacity - initial capacity of the byte buffer. It will grow (doubling, or to whatever a single event needs if larger) as needed and the grown capacity is kept for subsequent events.

      charset - charset to encode with.
